items.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998
items.q: my knowledge of languages made me a natural for the International Department... interest in standard music, you know the music of Gershwin, and Porter and Youmans and so forth.

ctx.x: Yesterday I had asked you a question about if the early jazz musicians thought of their music as an art form. And you said probably not.

No not really. They were just playing happy music that they had developed within their lives, and they were happy making a living at it as best they could in many cases of course. Because a jazz musician’s life has never been easy unless you happen to hit it big. But I don’t think musicians ever took it seriously as an art form until they were told it was an art form, and that probably started, I think it would have to be during the World War II years. Because before there weren’t any articles being written in…
It’s interesting that the music was considered enough of a popular entity that that would be something. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
